title: Aran twisted rib mittens
subtitle: Full mittens in aran weight with a twisted 1x1 rib that creates a neat, dense fabric.
excerpt: Full mittens in aran-weight wool, worked in twisted 1x1 rib (knitting into the back of each knit stitch). The twisted rib creates a denser, more structured fabric than standard rib and holds its shape through heavy use. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Twisted rib (k1 through back loop) is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), Barbara G. Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), and the Harmony Guide to Knitting Stitches (1982), among many other sources. Cross-referenced across 5 or more published works.

glossaryTerms.definition: Insert the right needle into the back of the stitch rather than the front, then knit normally. This twists the stitch and produces a tighter, more defined column. In twisted rib, every knit stitch is worked through the back loop.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in aran-weight wool, worked in twisted 1x1 rib where every knit stitch is worked
through the back loop
Afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Twisted rib knots each knit stitch so the column stands out more than in standard 1x1 rib. The fabric is denser and less elastic than plain rib, which makes it excellent for a mitten that needs to keep its shape through regular use. The aran weight works up quickly and the construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 110 g (200 m / 220 yards) of aran-weight wool per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 110 g (about 200 m / 220 yards) of aran-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4.5 mm (UK 7 / US 7) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 26 rounds to 10 cm in twisted 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 4.5 mm needles. The twisted rib swatch will be about 1 to 2 stitches per 10 cm tighter than plain rib at the same needle size; this is expected.
Twisted rib stitch

items.name: Every round
items.qty: *k1-tbl, p1*; repeat to end. All knit stitches are worked through the back loop. Purl stitches are worked normally.

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work twisted 1x1 rib for 24 (26, 28) rounds. The cuff measures about 9 (10, 11) cm.
Hand body

Continue in twisted 1x1 rib for 10 (12, 12) rounds. Place the thumb: work the first 9 (10, 11) stitches with waste yarn in rib pattern, slip back, and work in twisted rib to end. Continue for 18 (20, 22) more rounds.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint. Switch to plain stocking stitch for the decreases. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 9 (10, 11) stitches above and 9 (10, 11) below. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds of twisted 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Twisted rib looks like plain rib: the right needle was inserted into the front of the knit stitches instead of the back. The back-loop insertion pulls the stitch so it lies diagonally on the needle before knitting; the needle tip must pass behind the stitch.
Cast-on too tight: the long-tail cast-on at aran weight with small needles can be snug. Cast on over two needles held together and remove one before joining.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Twisted rib on a cabled aran mitten gives the same dense texture to the cuff and palm while the back uses a 6-stitch cable. The cabled aran mittens pattern uses the same needle size.
